entityDescription:
Created in 2000, the “Centro Tecnológico CTC”, is a non-profit private foundation recognised as an Official Technology Centre by Spain’s Competitivity and Economy Ministry. It is the only one in Cantabria’s region with this recognition.
CTC’s objective is to ad value and generate business to its clients through Research, Technological Development and Innovation. CTC is placed at experimental sciences and engineering fields, focused on:
- Navigation and Robotics
- Energy and Industry 
- Nano- and Advanced Materials
CTC leads navigation systems development for robotic applications. Among others, CTC develops advanced algorithms to improve reliability and autonomy of mobile robots and/or process. 
Thanks to its Navigation Laboratory, CTC can develop Navigation Systems, Stabilized Platforms and other “navigation sensor user” applications. The laboratory has relevant and high specialised capabilities in sensor and systems modelling and characterization.
NL has a 2 axis movement simulator ACUTRONIC SIMEX TWO with removable thermal camera, and pay loads up to 45 kg for modelling and calibration of MEMS inertial sensors and for stabilized platforms validation (Hardware-in-the Loop). It has as well experimental devices to develop position calculation GNSS systems and antennas calibration (Phase Centre Variation), including a 2 axis high precision rotation table.
CTC actively participated in several European and Spanish national projects in this field. For example, CTC leaded and coordinated H2020 Project “GREENPATROL”, in which an autonomous robotic solution was developed to detect and control pests inside greenhouses. Now, CTC coordinates another H2020 project, MooringSense. In this project CTC developes an intelligent sensor based on navigation systems.
CTC participate actively in national and international congresses related to mobile robotics and navigation systems and is part of several clusters and associations such as CapTech, Navegación, Guiado y Control de la Agencia Europea de Defensa.

The Fraunhofer IAPT is one of the leading institutions in the field of Additive Manufacturing (3D Printing). The focus is on the industrialization of additive manufacturing technologies and the associated technology transfer to enable completely new and resource-efficient products. Our additive experts stand for sustainable innovation in the field of additive production. This ranges from developments on the process and material level, the development of novel component designs and system technologies to factory planning and digitization.
The wide-ranging possibilities of additive manufacturing are particularly well suited for the aerospace industry. Weight-optimized parts, for example, have a positive effect on the overall mass of your aircraft. Flow-optimized parts improve the performance of rocket engines. In addition, hydraulic components can be designed to be much more efficient, creating advantages not only within the part itself, but also in conjunction with the overall system. Development times for prototypes can be reduced and downtime minimized by the availability of spare parts. In this way, additive manufacturing can be of great importance to space industry, especially when conventional manufacturing processes reach their limits because of component complexity or when time plays an overriding role due to the associated costs.

xSpectre AB was founded in August 2020 with the idea to explore developments in miniaturized (mini) spectrometers with the help of an innovative geometric-mathematical model engine. The surge in mini-spectrometers over the past years has led to a multitude of new applications and start-ups, now developing into an ecosystem of businesses and markets. The lions share of all applications rely on back-end (vendor) driven algorithms that translate a spectral signal to concentration or content, either using traditional methods including for instance Beer’s law, or modern Artificial Intelligence (AI). The solution usually entails a physical spectrometer that comes with a preinstalled (or online available) app that is dedicated to a particular application.

The spectrometer development by xSpectre AB is instead a general purpose sensor that comes with:
- exchangeable muzzles for different applications,

- possibilities to analyze solids, liquids and gases,

- abilities to analyze transmittance, absorbance, reflectance, fluorescence and Raman spectra,

- a mobile phone connected app used for control, communication and edge computing,

- an online (backend) cloud service for data management and spectral computing,

- a set of external probes that can be used for directly sensing physical and chemical sample properties together with with spectral sensing,

- a geometric-mathematical model engine that translates spectral signals to abundance,

- possibilities for domain experts to AI assisted development of novel models for translating spectral signals to abundances, and

- preparations for developing a user community.

A patent application has been handed in for the geometric-mathematical model engine to the Swedish Intellectual Property Office (application nr 2150075-6, 25 January 2021).

The first application under development with xSpectre’s handheld spectrometer is for analyzing and predicting soil properties. The Swedish Agency for Innovation Systems, VINNOVA, supported the initial development and we are now (October 2021) ready for tests at Technical Readiness Level (TRL) 7 - system prototype demonstration in operational environment. An initial market analysis has indicated that precision farming based on drone and satellite data (that usually lack sufficient local ground data for proper translation of multi-spectral data to biophysical properties) and emerging markets for AgTech and regenerative farming are the two most likely market segments where we initially can find partners.

entityName: WSL Swiss Federal Institute for Forest, Snow and Landscape Research
entityDescription: The Swiss Federal Institute for Forest, Snow and Landscape Research is concerned with the use, development and protection of natural and urban spaces. The focus of our research is on solving problems to do with the responsible use of landscapes and forests and a prudent approach to natural hazards, especially those common in mountainous countries. WSL occupies a leading position internationally in these research areas. We also provide groundwork for sustainable environmental policies in Switzerland. WSL has, from the start, been active in all regions in Switzerland. In 1888 the first experimental plots were set up across the country to find out more about tree growth and yield. Today WSL maintains more than 6000 experimental and research plots, including large experimental stations for studying rock fall or debris flow, study areas for monitoring the effects of climate change on forests and sites damaged by storms or fires for investigating the impact of these natural hazards. WSL is a research institute of the Swiss Confederation. It is part of the ETH Domain and employs approximately 500 people. In addition to the headquarters in Birmensdorf, near Zurich, and to the WSL Institute for Snow and Avalanche Research SLF in Davos, branch stations in Lausanne and Cadenazzo and Sion generate local synergies and reach out to professionals.
